lead: Brow slitting, also called eyebrow slits or brow cuts, is a grooming style in which one or more thin lines are shaved or trimmed through the eyebrow hair so that a bare strip of skin shows in a short vertical or diagonal gap. People use it as a styling accent: the gap draws attention to the brow and eye area and gives the face a deliberate, edgy look. It is a hair-styling choice, usually done with a razor or trimmer, and it does not involve cutting skin.

Wikipedia's general article on eyebrows notes that shaving lines into the eyebrows was a cosmetic trend among some younger people in the 1990s and 2000s, and cites a 2008 news report that linked the trend to gang concerns in schools.[1] Beyond that mention, little encyclopedic or scientific material exists on the style itself, so this article is short.

angle.text: The slit is a visible styling detail that changes the brow outline and stands out around the eyes. Because only hair is removed, the effect is temporary and the brow grows back.

paras: The style removes a narrow strip of hair across the brow, most often near the tail or arch, leaving a visible gap. Variations include a single slit, multiple slits, or a diagonal cut. Because only hair is removed, the gap fills in as the hair regrows.

Brow shaping more broadly is a long-established practice, and fashions in eyebrow shape have changed repeatedly: Japanese hikimayu from the 8th century involved shaving or plucking brows and painting them higher on the forehead, Elizabethan high-status women sometimes removed brows entirely, and thin plucked brows returned in the 1920s and 1930s.[1] Modern options include tweezing, waxing, threading, trimming, makeup, microblading and transplants.[1]

Wikipedia describes the brows as important to communication, since mobile brows convey emotions such as surprise, recognition and sympathy, and says brow styles reflect the aesthetic ideals of their time.[1] Slits are one of the youth-led variations within that history.

The Wikipedia article on eyebrows reports that shaved lines in the brow were popular among some younger people in the 1990s and 2000s, and mentions a 2008 news report connecting the look to gang-related concerns in schools.[1] The article gives no further detail on how widely such associations were held.

Brow slits are generally treated in appearance communities as a style choice rather than a facial-structure change. Discussion of eyebrows in looksmaxxing spaces more often concerns shape, density and the eye area, and no published studies examine how slits affect perceived attractiveness.

quick.overview:
Brow slitting is a grooming style where a thin line of hair is shaved out of the eyebrow. It has been popular with some young people since at least the 1990s and is a fashion choice rather than a structural change.

Sources on the style are thin. Encyclopedias mention it only briefly, and no studies have tested its effect on how a face is perceived.
quick.mechanism: Hair is trimmed or shaved from a narrow strip of the brow with a razor or trimmer, leaving bare skin visible. Nothing is done to the skin or follicle, so the gap grows back.
quick.risks: Shaving carries the usual minor risks of razor use such as nicks or irritation. A 2008 news report cited by Wikipedia linked the style to gang concerns in some schools, which can matter where school or workplace dress rules apply.
